note: EIP Appendix H 11818 path-scope corpus for the two existing MOD-004 rules. Representative matching and non-matching paths, both directions required: positives alone would qualify a glob of '**', negatives alone would qualify an empty glob set. 'declared_paths' pins the globs each rule declared when this corpus was written, so a later widening of a rule's scope fails the corpus instead of passing it silently. This corpus qualifies the DECLARED globs under the semantics in rule_scope.py; it does not exercise Claude Code's own rule matcher and no RULE evidence ID follows from it.

rules.must_match_note: The four representative paths RULE-001's record names, plus nested forms. None of these files exists yet: all four declared directories are absent, so the globs are forward-looking.
rules.must_not_match_note: Three groups. (1) The published S0 slice, which contracts/engineering/mod004-s0-capability.json already asserts is outside both rule globs -- re-checked here rather than restated. (2) Prefix near-misses, which a startswith() implementation would wrongly match. (3) Unrelated contexts, which 11818 calls pollution.

rules.must_match_note: RULE-002's single glob is described by the rule file itself as a non-operative provisional placeholder that 'matches no existing repository path'. These paths exercise the glob; none exists, and there is no frontend/ directory at all, so the rule file's own claim holds and `check` reports it.
rules.must_not_match_note: CON-01/02/03 belong to MOD-029 and MOD-031 per the rule file, so reaching them would be exactly the pollution 11818 tests for. The bare directory path is excluded because a trailing /** selects what is below a directory, not the directory itself.
